subject.title: Feature/Fix: Integrate lineage discovery and shadow accounting

question: Should CodexBar adopt this four-PR lineage-ledger architecture, or prefer the narrower identity and cache-invalidation approach in https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2118?
rationale: Both approaches address the same active overcount investigation but establish different long-term accounting boundaries; code review cannot safely choose the permanent scanner architecture or stack order without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt the lineage stack
options.body: Merge the foundation first, reconcile the overlap with the narrower fix, and require exact-head runtime and refresh-cost proof before landing this integration layer.

options.title: Prefer the narrower fix
options.body: Prioritize the proven identity and cache-invalidation repair and pause this stack until remaining overcount evidence demonstrates that a lineage ledger is still necessary.

options.title: Request a consolidated proposal
options.body: Have the overlapping contributors produce one smaller architecture that preserves the proven cache fix and introduces shadow accounting behind a bounded integration seam.

recommendation.title: Adopt the lineage stack
recommendation.body: Merge the foundation first, reconcile the overlap with the narrower fix, and require exact-head runtime and refresh-cost proof before landing this integration layer.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice sets the long-term accounting architecture and integration order for the repository's central Codex scanner.
